summary: Interpreted the user-restore receipt and closed the repair question's second mechanism. Receipt 6ff0ef691a0141449142bfa06719bb47 evaluated all five comparisons: the leader's public Restore call succeeded once its FSM had caught up (holds, index 5), the restarted node's applied writes became the snapshot's majority write (holds, index 5), its minority write was gone (holds, index 5), all five nodes' applied write lists agreed afterwards (holds, index 5), and the feature-off control was equally consistent (holds, index 12) — the cluster-wide convergence the per-node installSnapshot path did not reach. The experiment-level interpretation is holds with no defect judgment of its own, the repair question now records both mechanisms with their scopes (per-node install for a node that falls behind a compacted leader; cluster-wide convergence when the leader consumes a snapshot through Restore) and keeps the term-changing truncation path as its one unexercised mechanism, the child and parent limitation lists were corrected to drop the unexercised-user-Restore claim, and the follower-side snapshot knowledge entry gained this receipt plus an updated trigger condition. Incomplete: the term-changing truncation path, and the alternative reachability story for the constructor stall in which a node's snapshots fail rather than being merely delayed — the next thing I intend to probe within the remaining budget.
